text:
maria: quick update — ran a microbench on the http2 small-frame path this morning. high-level: ~18% extra host CPU when requests arrive as many tiny frames (~<512B) and kv-cache miss rate climbs.

aj: oof. is that the preparse stage or the framing layer?

maria: mostly preparse + tokenization. trace shows repeated re-allocs and syscall churn in the parse loop when frames arrive fragmented. also kernel selection for tiny decode workloads chooses a 'wide' kernel that doesn't like small seq lengths.

lucas: can you paste the flame or top snippet?

maria: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# perf top (host preparse)
7.2%  parse::try_accumulate_frames
6.8%  tokenize::utf8_to_utf16
6.1%  sys_readv
5.5%  grpc::slice_sync_copy
4.2%  kernel::decode_dispatch_wide
```

shen: that decode_dispatch_wide is the one we've seen favoring batch-size>64, right? small frames push it into a less efficient code path.

aj: yeah, kernel hysteresis — we bias to 'wide' kernels if recent sequences were long to avoid jitter, but it backfires on suddenly small-frame traffic.

maria: exactly. for this workload the traffic is bursty: long chats then lots of short tool calls with tiny payloads. kills CPU and increases tail P99 by ~25ms.

lucas: what's the kv-cache behavior here? miss amplification?

maria: kv cache has thrash: when small frames come in, the parsing stride fragments the KV keys we use for prefix caching, reducing hit rate. we see increased memcmp cost and bucket splits.

aj: rough idea for mitigations?

maria: proposed quick wins: 1) lower kernel hysteresis threshold for http2 ingress (switch to prefer narrow kernel for seq_len median < 32), 2) add a fast-path preparse for micro-frames that avoids a full UTF conversion until we have full token boundary, 3) coalesce small GRPC slices before parse (we already have writev on egress, do similar on ingress).

shen: any risk to decoder quality/latency? the hysteresis tweak could cause oscillation.

maria: risk matrix: small. we can add a cooldown window (200ms) to avoid flip-flop and measure. also fallback to current wide kernel if throughput > X tokens/s.

dev-bot: deploy-candidate built: sha=ab12c3, bench-suite=ingress-smallframe. Results: baseline CPU=1.00, candidate CPU=0.82, median latency -6ms, p99 -22ms.

lucas: nice. can we get a run with kvcache hit-rate instrumentation (per-route) on for a day?

maria: yes, enabling per-route kv metrics for the canary, will collect for 24h. also adding a log tag for coalesced frames so we can correlate.

aj: thanks. if the canary looks good, let's ship to dedicated pool only first. no global rollout until kv hit-rate stable. :thumbsup:

shen: one more ask — can we add a stressbench that alternates long seqs and tiny-frame bursts to validate no regressions?

maria: will add to perf harness (script name: perf/ingress_mix_burst.sh). attaching the shell snippet here: 
```bash
# perf/ingress_mix_burst.sh
for i in {1..100}; do
  # long chat window
  ./client --seq 1024 --rate 200 --duration 10s
  # short tool bursts
  for j in {1..50}; do
    ./client --seq 12 --frame-size 256 --rate 100 --duration 0.2s
  done
done
```

aj: perfect. schedule the canary tomorrow 09:00 PT. I'll watch the dashboards.

maria: thanks team. I'll push the PR for hysteresis + coalesce today and link the canary when it's up.

lucas: appreciate the concise plan.

maria: fyi logs will include: `ingress.coalesced=true` and `kvroute.hit_after_coalesce=true|false` so we can slice results.
